Extend $BA$ to point $Q$ such that $AQ=2AP$, and $CQ$, $DP$ intersect at point $T$. When point $P$ moves from point $A$ to the right towards point $B$, what is the length of the path traced by point $T$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Extend $AT$ until it intersects $CD$ at $N$, as shown in the diagram: \\
Since $CD\parallel BQ$,\\
it follows that $ \frac{AP}{DN} = \frac{AT}{NT} = \frac{AQ}{CN}$,\\
therefore, $ \frac{AP}{AQ} = \frac{1}{2} = \frac{DN}{CN}$,\\
thus, point $N$ is the trisection point on $CD$ closer to $D$,\\
hence, point $T$ moves along segment $AN$,\\
when $P$ moves from point $A$ to the right until it coincides with $B$, as depicted in the diagram: \\
the path of point $T$ is along $AT$, draw $DH\perp AB$ at $H$, and draw $TM\perp AB$ at $M$,\\
in $\triangle ADH$, $\tan \angle DAB = \frac{4}{3}$,\\
let $DH = 4k$, then $AH = 3k$, $AD = 5k$,\\
since $AD = AB = 3$,\\
it follows that $5k = 3$,\\
thus, $k = \frac{3}{5}$,\\
therefore, $DH = \frac{12}{5}$, $AH = \frac{9}{5}$,\\
thus, $BH = AB - AH = \frac{6}{5}$,\\
since $ \frac{DT}{PT} = \frac{CD}{PQ} = \frac{AP}{AP+AQ} = \frac{1}{3}$,\\
it follows that $ \frac{PT}{PD} = \frac{3}{4}$,\\
since $DH\perp AB$, $TM\perp AB$,\\
it follows that $TM\parallel DH$,\\
hence, $ \frac{PT}{PD} = \frac{TM}{DH} = \frac{BM}{BH}$, namely $ \frac{3}{4} = \frac{TM}{\frac{12}{5}} = \frac{BM}{\frac{6}{5}}$,\\
thus, $TM = \frac{9}{5}$, $BM = \frac{9}{10}$,\\
therefore, $AM = AB - BM = \frac{21}{10}$,\\
in $\triangle ATM$, $AT = \sqrt{AM^{2}+TM^{2}} = \boxed{\frac{3\sqrt{85}}{10}}$.

When point $P$ moves from point $A$ to the right towards point $B$, what is the length of the path traced by point $T$?

\textbf{Solution:} Extend $AT$ until it intersects $CD$ at $N$, as shown in the diagram: \\
Since $CD\parallel BQ$,\\
it follows that $ \frac{AP}{DN} = \frac{AT}{NT} = \frac{AQ}{CN}$,\\
therefore, $ \frac{AP}{AQ} = \frac{1}{2} = \frac{DN}{CN}$,\\
thus, point $N$ is the trisection point on $CD$ closer to $D$,\\
hence, point $T$ moves along segment $AN$,\\
when $P$ moves from point $A$ to the right until it coincides with $B$, as depicted in the diagram: \\
the path of point $T$ is along $AT$, draw $DH\perp AB$ at $H$, and draw $TM\perp AB$ at $M$,\\
in $\triangle ADH$, $\tan \angle DAB = \frac{4}{3}$,\\
let $DH = 4k$, then $AH = 3k$, $AD = 5k$,\\
since $AD = AB = 3$,\\
it follows that $5k = 3$,\\
thus, $k = \frac{3}{5}$,\\
therefore, $DH = \frac{12}{5}$, $AH = \frac{9}{5}$,\\
thus, $BH = AB - AH = \frac{6}{5}$,\\
since $ \frac{DT}{PT} = \frac{CD}{PQ} = \frac{AP}{AP+AQ} = \frac{1}{3}$,\\
it follows that $ \frac{PT}{PD} = \frac{3}{4}$,\\
since $DH\perp AB$, $TM\perp AB$,\\
it follows that $TM\parallel DH$,\\
hence, $ \frac{PT}{PD} = \frac{TM}{DH} = \frac{BM}{BH}$, namely $ \frac{3}{4} = \frac{TM}{\frac{12}{5}} = \frac{BM}{\frac{6}{5}}$,\\
